script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

- South Asia: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations.
- Africa: Sudan experiences massive power outages after RSF drone strikes.
- Western Russia: Russians strike Yasnohirka in Donetsk Oblast: one killed, teenager among injured – photo.

Full breakdown follows.

Russian forces carried out four strikes on the town of Yasnohirka in Donetsk Oblast on the morning of 26 October, leaving one person dead and ten others injured, including a teenage girl.

One person was killed when Russian forces attacked the city of Pavlohrad in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast with a drone on Monday 26 October.

Ukrainian forces have hit the Energiya plant in Lipetsk Oblast, degrading Russia's supply of specialised power units for glide bomb modules and ballistic missiles.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations.
The Foreign Office (FO) on Monday rejected allegations made by the Afghan Taliban government regarding civilian casualties in Islamabad’s counterterrorism campaign in the neighbouring country, maintaining that Pakistan’s conduct always “reflected restraint” and the response was “proportionate to the level of threat”. The Afghan Taliban have repeatedly claimed civilian casualties in Pakistani strikes in Afghanistan; Pakistani authorities have denied the accusations, holding that they target military and terrorist infrastructure.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, ABC News Australia, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Jordan arrests 3 in dawn raid over church attack.
Jordanian security forces on Monday arrested three suspects over an attack on a church last week that killed nine people, with the trio wounded in a dawn raid and shootout, authorities said. The kingdom’s Public Security Directorate said the group were apprehended at an abandoned house where they had barricaded themselves inside and opened fire on security forces. One of the suspects was taken to hospital in critical condition, while the other two were stable, Jordan’s state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka reported. There were no casualties among security forces, it added.
- The Hindu - International, South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Intercepted missile after Houthis hit Riyadh airport, says Saudi coalition.
The Houthis have carried out waves of strikes on the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and injured more than 300
- Dawn (Pakistan), 7 hours ago: Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks targeting Makkah, Madina as 'grave violation' of Saudi sovereignty.
Pakistan on Monday condemned Houthi missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s Makkah and Madina regions, terming them a “grave violation” of the kingdom’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. According to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO), these “reprehensible attacks constitute a grave violation of Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and demonstrate a blatant disregard for the sanctity of Islam’s holiest sites and the safety of civilians”. Pakistan reiterated its “unwavering solidarity” with Saudi Arabia and its firm commitment to the Makkah Alliance, the FO said.

Navy chief Admiral Krishna Swaminathan underlines the urgency for rapid innovation to boost operational efficiency, while Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar highlights how the ongoing Ukraine conflict exemplifies the fast-evolving nature of warfare driven by tech advancements.

An 18-year-old boy, along with his father and friend, faced a shocking assault in Kolkata after he was caught kissing his underage girlfriend. The girl's family allegedly threatened them and forced the couple to parade without clothes. This incident sparked outrage among local residents, leading to vandalism at the suspects' home and clashes with police forces. Authorities have since arrested three individuals, including the girl's parents and uncle.
